attempted_claim: Let M_{c,d} = d^2/dx^2 - (x^6 + c*x^4 + d*x^2) over C(x) with constants C, with parameters (c,d) in all of C^2 (even sextic oscillator; no finite singularities, sole singularity an unramified irregular point at infinity of rank 4 with 8 Stokes directions and x -> -x symmetry). Compute the formal fundamental matrix at infinity (exponential parts of degree 4, formal monodromy, exponential torus), the eight Stokes matrices, and run the Kovacic reduction over C(x) including symmetric-power bounds. Decide with proof for every (c,d) in C^2 the connected differential Galois group G^0(M_{c,d}): either G^0 = SL(2,C) or a named proper connected subgroup, giving the exact exceptional locus in the (c,d)-plane (including any quasi-exactly-solvable algebraic curves) and identifying the Stokes-matrix witness pattern generating G^0 with the formal data. A complete answer is the explicit Stokes-matrix list plus a theorem proving this SL(2,C)-versus-exceptional dichotomy with no further exceptions.
claim_type: SL2-versus-exceptional connected Galois dichotomy with Stokes witnesses
decisive_failure: The literal target required a finite closed-form Stokes-matrix list for all of C^2 plus an exhaustive dichotomy proof; Stokes multipliers are transcendental in (c,d) and the QES exceptional locus is infinite, so completeness was unreachable in the bounded pass and no independently auditable alternative remained.
